result.title: Accessed, never disclosed: Silent access to protected health information by medical artificial intelligence agents
result.comment: 33 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, 3 Extended Data tables; includes Supplementary Information (12 tables, 6 figures)
result.summary: Medical artificial intelligence agents should retrieve patient identifiers only when a task requires them, the data-minimization principle behind the HIPAA minimum necessary standard for protected health information (PHI). An agent can retrieve identifiers without revealing them. Such silent access remains invisible to evaluations that inspect only the output. We embedded canaries in synthetic patient records and linked each tool invocation to canary exposure in the final answers across five language models, four boundary levels, and seven attack frames for identifier-free clinical tasks. Three models invoked the PHI tools unnecessarily, whereas Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 did not. Stronger boundaries reduced this access, and the residual access under the strictest policy was confined to frames in which the user overrode the policy or asserted approval. A pre-execution gate given the task-necessity criterion nearly eliminated this access. Output-only evaluation cannot verify minimum-necessary access; boundaries, gates, and access-log audits are required together.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在合成病历中植入 canary，跨五个模型、四种边界与七种攻击框架，检验医疗智能体是否在无需身份信息的临床任务中静默调用 PHI 工具，并评估执行前门控与访问日志审计能否约束这类「可见于访问、不可见于输出」的行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「canary 暴露追踪 + 工具调用审计」把输出中看不见但内部确实发生的信息访问显式化，可能可供核查 latent 推理是否真正读取了特定视觉细节一类问题；但对象为医疗文本智能体，与视觉推理无直接联系。
